release_infrastructure.risk_description: This task changes the production release mechanism and container lifecycle ownership. Misconfiguration could disconnect Caddy, start a second polling Worker, replace an out-of-scope service, or create an unrecoverable production state. Restrict Kamal to API and Worker, keep external data services untouched, verify all runtime identities, and fail closed on mismatches.
release_infrastructure.backup_plan: Before any production Apply, obtain a fresh PostgreSQL backup using the existing production backup procedure and prove restore in an isolated PostgreSQL environment. Do not run database migrations unless separately authorized with exact migration contract and backup/restore evidence. Preserve current service image digests and Compose baseline.
release_infrastructure.rollback_plan: Use the prior verified container image identity with Kamal rollback only after a read-only baseline confirms the previous version and dependencies remain healthy. Keep PostgreSQL, Redis, Caddy and volumes unchanged. If runtime state or digest is ambiguous, stop for read-only reconciliation rather than retrying Apply.
stop_conditions: Stop if current production SHA or Docker digests differ from the authorization baseline without a reviewed continuation.
Stop before Apply if backup restore, Caddy routing, exact digest, Worker single-poller transition, health, lock, or rollback readiness is not proven.
Stop immediately if the prior poller may still be running, a non-target service would be recreated, or Apply has an uncertain result.
